rationale:
The requirement has four obligations. The trait exposes `search_structure(source, rule) -> Result<Vec<Span>, OutlineError>`. It returns matched byte ranges within the supplied source. The default implementation returns an unsupported-language error. Plain text supplies outlining only. The reviewed tests cover each of them.

- **Default unsupported error.** `outline_only_languages_report_unsupported_structural_search` uses `CustomLanguage`, which does not override `search_structure`. It asserts that `search_structure` fails with a message containing "unsupported". That exercises the trait default. In `contents.rs`, the default returns `unsupported_search(self.name())`, whose message contains "unsupported".
- **Plain text is outlining only.** The same test calls `languages::PlainText.search_structure` and asserts that it returns an error whose message contains "plain-text". This is the language-specific unsupported error: the message names the language. The check is a bit loose, since the test does not also assert "unsupported" for plain text, but the error path is exercised and asserted.
- **Matched byte ranges within the supplied source.** `bundled_structural_search_returns_matches_and_rejects_bad_rules_and_source` runs a Rust `kind: function_item` rule over two functions. It asserts that the exact slices `source[*range]` are `"fn first() {}"` and `"fn second() {}"`, so the ranges are correct byte ranges. `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline` runs a regex rule for all eight bundled structural languages. It asserts non-empty results and that every range slices into the source. The eight languages are Rust, Python, TypeScript, Tsx, Markdown, Css, Toml and Yaml.
- **Signature and error type.** Every test calls the method with `&str` source and a `serde_json::Map` rule and unwraps a `Vec<Span>` or an `OutlineError`. This fixes the trait signature at compile time. The bad-rule case and the unparsable-source case (`"fn {"`) are asserted to be errors. The requirement does not name these cases, so they are extra coverage.

I found no obligation that lacks a test and no plausible requirement-violating behavior that these assertions would accept. There are no {fixme} acknowledgments to account for.
